cases.reason: The reader said 'RD only', but the RD is only where the clause sits. The format's identifier-1 is an operand, and 2002 SR2 limits it only to an alphanumeric item that is not variable-length; it sets no section limit. So in 2002, identifier-1 may name an item of a record description entry that follows a CD (A.1.1.2), or an implicit CD data-name (SYMBOLIC DESTINATION, X(12)). The communication section does not exist in 2023, so the row's witnesses (pb1129_rd_code_literal and pb1129_rd_code_identifier, both working-storage) cannot reach that operand. This is the same reach that u-13's refuter used to overturn 2002-SR-13.16.12.2-2. Re-run here: code_cd.cob (RD CODE IS CD-CODE, a PIC X item of the record under an output CD) compiles at --std 2002 with only the COBOL0903 obsolete warning and prints 'QDD' (the code character precedes the line). At 2023 it is refused (COBOL0902).

Format 2's identifier-1 sections exclude the communication section in both editions (SR12), and Format 2 is screen-only and licensed in 2002. pb1220 runs at 2002.

cases.reason: The format IS EXTERNAL [AS literal-1] is identical, but the places it may be written differ. 2002 SR1 admits it 'in record description entries in the working-storage section', and a 2002 record description entry is the whole set of data description entries of a record (13.10). So the 2002 words admit EXTERNAL on a subordinate (level 2-49) WS entry, and 2002 13.14.2 SR7 ('any entry containing the ... EXTERNAL clause') presupposes such entries. 2014 E.2 confirms that the 2002 rule opened this case. 2023 SR1 restricts the clause to level 1 entries. The reader's scope, 'a working-storage record description entry', was checked only at level 1 (pb511, ext_fd.cob). Probe ext05ok.cob (01 WR. 05 XA PIC X(4) IS EXTERNAL.) is refused at --std 2002 with COBOL2404, citing §2023:13.18.22.3 SR1, a rule the 2002 text does not contain. The same overturn was made for 2002-SR-13.16.20.2-2 and 2002-SR-13.14.2-7 (p-10). A counter-reading exists: 2002 8.x 'external attribute' speaks of a record given the attribute 'by the presence of the EXTERNAL clause in its data description entry'. It is not decisive against SR1's words plus the 2014 E.2 statement, so this is refuted by default. Related: u-14 found a second 2002-only case reachable through this format, a strongly-typed record under an EXTERNAL FD, refused by the 2023-only 13.18.22.3 SR5.
